Article Title: Google’s Android earthquake alerts expand to 200+ regions with more info; Sundar Pichai explains how it helped in Venezuela
Article Text:
New details added to earthquake alerts

Designed to provide precious seconds of warning

Google has announced a major expansion of its Android Earthquake Alerts System, extending the feature from 98 countries and regions to more than 200 while introducing additional information in earthquake warnings to help users respond more effectively during emergencies. The company also added that the system has managed to deliver more than one billion earthquake alerts since its launch in 2021, making it what Google describes as the world’s largest mobile-based earthquake detection network. The expanded coverage will bring alerts to more locations including Panama and Guatemala, among others.The announcement was highlighted by Google CEO Sundar Pichai, who said the technology has already aided people during critical moments. In a post on X, Pichai noted that the system has sent over one billion alerts since 2021 and is now expanding from 98 to nearly 200 countries and regions. He also pointed to this year's earthquakes in Venezuela, saying millions of people outside the epicentre received alerts and were able to take cover before the shaking began. “Since launching in 2021, our Android Earthquake Alerts System has sent 1B+ alerts. Now we’re expanding the system from 98 to nearly 200 countries and regions.Proud how this technology can help in moments that really matter. As one example, when the devastating earthquakes hit Venezuela this year, millions of people outside the epicenter got alerts and could take cover before the shaking began,” wrote Pichai in a post.Alongside the geographic expansion, Google is enhancing its "Be Ready" earthquake alert with more contextual information. In the coming months, users will see a map showing the radius of detected shaking, the estimated earthquake magnitude, recommended actions, and a button to access more information as details become available.Android users in supported regions may receive one of three alert types depending on the expected intensity of shaking. The "Be Aware" alert is designed for estimated light shaking, while "Be Ready" provides advance notice of stronger shaking and encourages users to prepare. The highest-level "Take Action" alert appears full-screen and offers immediate safety guidance for moderate to heavy shaking.Google said even a few seconds of advance notice can be crucial during an earthquake, giving people time to take cover and protect themselves. The Android Earthquake Alerts System uses mobile devices to help detect seismic activity and deliver warnings before strong shaking reaches users.The company said its safety-focused products play an important role during natural disasters, adding that the latest expansion aims to provide more people with potentially life-saving information when they need it most.
Article Summary: Google has announced a major expansion of its Android Earthquake Alerts System, extending the feature from 98 countries and regions to more than 200. The company added that the system has managed to deliver more than one billion earthquake alerts since its launch in 2021. The expanded coverage will bring alerts to more locations including Panama and Guatemala, among others.

Article Title: Meta releases Muse Spark Open AI model with 816 billion parameters; runs on two Apple Mac Studios
Article Text:
Meta releases Muse Spark Open AI model with 816 billion parameters; runs on two Apple Mac Studios

Meta Muse Spark Open: Features and capabilities

How to access Muse Spark Open AI model

Meta has released Muse Spark Open, an open-weight artificial intelligence (AI) model designed for coding, complex reasoning and tasks that require multiple steps. The company says the model can run on a desktop setup using two Apple Mac Studios powered by M5 Ultra chips, making it possible to use an advanced AI model locally rather than relying only on cloud services. As stated by the company in its official announcement, Muse Spark Open has 816 billion total parameters, with 42 billion active parameters, and supports a context window of 1 million tokens. Developers can access the model through several AI platforms or download its weights to customize it for their needs.Meta said Muse Spark Open is designed for long-running tasks, complex software development and agentic AI workflows, in which a model can carry out multiple steps towards a goal.The model is natively multimodal, meaning it can work with different types of information. It has 816 billion total parameters, of which 42 billion are active, and a context window of 1 million tokens. A large context window allows a model to process a substantial amount of information in a single interaction.Meta said it tested the model on tasks involving software development and video editing. In one test, the model was used to make bug fixes and add features to Ice Cubes, an open-source Mastodon client, before building the application.In another, it worked with DaVinci Resolve to review video footage frame by frame, identify suitable moments and crop clips into a vertical format.The company also said the model includes optimised GPU kernels that deliver kernel-level speed improvements of 1.03 to 3.95 times on NVIDIA and AMD GPUs. Meta reported a 3% overall speed improvement on AMD MI350.Meta says Muse Spark Open is available through AI inference platforms including Baseten, Fireworks AI, Groq, Modal, Nebius, OpenRouter and Together AI. Developers can download its model weights through Hugging Face, Amazon SageMaker AI, Google Cloud Model Garden and Microsoft Foundry Models. The model supports inference engines such as SGLang, vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, Hugging Face Transformers, Apple MLX, llama.cpp and Unsloth. Developers can also customise it using PyTorch.For local use, Meta has optimised Muse Spark Open for Apple's M5 Ultra Mac Studio through the MLX framework. According to the company, two Mac Studios can work together to provide enough unified memory to hold the model.Meta said it has added safety training to the open-weight version and evaluated it under its Superintelligence Scaling Framework. The company said the model met the safety thresholds required for release.The model is being released under the Muse Model License, which allows many developers to use it for free but includes limited commercial terms. Its weights are available through the Muse Spark Open collection on Hugging Face.
Article Summary: Muse Spark Open is designed for coding, complex reasoning and tasks that require multiple steps. The model is natively multimodal, meaning it can work with different types of information. It has 816 billion total parameters, of which 42 billion are active, and a context window of 1 million tokens.

Article Title: Years after telling Meta employees to inflict pain on Apple, Mark Zuckerberg sends 'thanks note' to Apple CEO John Ternus; gets a 'reply'
Article Text:
Apple and Meta are on speaking terms again

Meta's most capable open AI model now runs on Apple's Mac Studio

Apple's privacy push cost Meta billions and sparked years of barbs

A former Apple executive helped bring Meta and Apple back to the table

Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg has publicly thanked Apple 's new CEO John Ternus , and Ternus has written back. The exchange happened on X on Thursday, when Meta released the weights for Muse Spark Open. That's Meta's new open-weight AI model, and the two companies spent months tuning it to run locally on Apple's Mac Studio desktops. Zuckerberg shared a picture of Meta's AI agent at work on a Mac. He wrote that the model "runs great on new Mac Studios thanks to work with @johnternus and Apple."Ternus took over from Tim Cook last month. He replied "Congrats to the team!" and said Mac Studio "keeps pushing the boundaries of on-device AI." It is a far cry from 2021. That year, Apple's App Tracking Transparency feature hit Facebook's ad business, and Zuckerberg reportedly told employees the company needed to "inflict pain" on Apple.Muse Spark Open is an 816-billion-parameter model built on a mixture-of-experts design. Meta calls it the most capable US-developed open-weight model to date. It is aimed at long coding sessions, multi-step reasoning and video analysis. The model is free to download from platforms like Hugging Face, and its licence allows commercial use with some limits.The setup links two or four Mac Studios running Apple's M5 Ultra chip.Apple's MLX framework splits the model across those machines. Apple has also put out new benchmarks and technical notes on how MLX handles open models of this size. Since everything stays on the desk, Meta does not see the prompts or files developers feed it. "Meta has no control or visibility to any of that," Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang said.It does not come cheap. An M5 Ultra Mac Studio with 256GB of memory costs over Rs 9 lakh at US prices, and the model needs at least two. A 512GB version is due later this month.The bad blood goes back years. In 2018, at the height of the Cambridge Analytica scandal, Cook was asked what he would do in Zuckerberg's shoes. "I wouldn't be in this situation," he said. Zuckerberg called the remark "extremely glib."Then iOS 14.5 arrived in 2021. It made apps ask permission before tracking users across other apps and websites, and most iPhone owners chose not to be tracked. Meta later estimated the change would cut its 2022 revenue by $10 billion. As recently as last year, Zuckerberg told podcaster Joe Rogan that Apple "hasn't invented anything great since the iPhone."The two have not struck a public partnership since 2017, when Apple pulled Facebook's built-in integration from iOS.Wang credits Daniel Gross with getting the two sides to work together. Gross is a former Apple executive who joined Meta's AI push last year. "Most of the animosity predates my tenure at the company," Wang said in an interview. He added that he was "excited for mommy and daddy to be playing nice again."Both sides get something here. Apple gets to show its chips can handle heavy AI work away from Nvidia-powered data centres. Meta gets its model in front of developers who might later pay to scale up. Apple already uses Google's Gemini models in Apple Intelligence, and its relationship with OpenAI has ended up in court.Neither company would say if more is coming. The real test would be Meta's models showing up inside Apple Intelligence. For now, the change is mostly one of tone. Five years after talking about inflicting pain on Apple, Zuckerberg is tagging its CEO by name, and Ternus is replying with exclamation marks.
Article Summary: Meta's most capable open-weight AI model now runs on Apple's Mac Studio. Zuckerberg shared a picture of Meta's AI agent at work on a Mac. He wrote that the model "runs great on new Mac Studios thanks to work with @johnternus and Apple"

Article Title: An Ohio wetland was taken over by invasive reeds in 2000; by 2022, cattails and other wetland plants had become dominant
Article Text:
Representative Image of coastal wetland restoration in Metzger Marsh, Ohio, highlighting 27 years of plant changes ( AI Generrated Image)

Metzger Marsh restoration: why the dike was built

From mudflat vegetation to invasive common reed

Cattails and other wetland plants dominate by 2022

What the long-term record shows

A wetland in the western Lake Erie region of Ohio offers researchers a long-term record of vegetation changes following restoration. In a study titled The Metzger marsh restoration—a vegetation-centric look after 27 years published in the Journal of Great Lakes Research in its April 2024 issue, Douglas A. Wilcox, Kurt P. Kowalski and Alexandra A. Bozimowski examined Metzger Marsh using vegetation records spanning 1994 to 2022. The research traces changes after a dike was built in 1995 to replace a protective barrier beach that had eroded. Water levels were lowered the following year, and the vegetation changed over the years that followed. By 2000, invasive common reed had become dominant, while later management measures reduced its extent. By 2022, cattails and other wetland plants were dominant. The findings document the changing plant communities recorded during the restoration project.Metzger Marsh is a coastal wetland in the western Lake Erie region of Ohio, near the Ottawa National Wildlife Refuge and the Metzger Marsh State Wildlife Area. The restoration project was designed to recover a 300-hectare wetland that had deteriorated following the loss of its protective barrier beach.In 1995, a dike was constructed to replace the function of the eroded barrier. Unlike a structure that would completely separate the marsh from the lake, it incorporated a water-control mechanism to allow managers to regulate the connection between the two. A passage for fish was incorporated into the structure, with the design intended to limit the movement of large common carp into the marsh. The researchers examined vegetation before, during and after construction. Their analysis used colour-infrared aerial photographs from 1994 to 2010, together with imagery from 2022. They also carried out quantitative sampling of major vegetation types. These records provided a basis for comparing the plant communities at different stages of the restoration.The first recorded changes followed a reduction in water levels in 1996. According to the researchers, the drawdown prompted plants to emerge from the soil’s seed bank, including species associated with exposed mudflats. Tree seedlings also appeared. More than half of the marsh was vegetated during this early period and in subsequent years. The study records the water-control structure opening in 1998. By 2000, invasive Phragmites australis, or common reed, had become the marsh’s dominant plant. Its spread marked a substantial change in the vegetation recorded during the project.The study also records that herbicide use and flooding eliminated most of the trees. Management measures subsequently reduced the area occupied by Phragmites. The sequence matters because the vegetation observed during the first years after the dike was built differed from that found later. Mudflat plants and tree seedlings appeared after the drawdown, followed by the spread of invasive common reed. Subsequent management was accompanied by a reduction in the reed’s extent.By 2022, Typha species, commonly called cattails, had become dominant alongside broadleaf arrowhead (Sagittaria latifolia) and softstem bulrush (Schoenoplectus tabernaemontani). These plants formed the dominant vegetation recorded at the end of the study period, in contrast with the prominence of invasive Phragmites around 2000.The authors concluded that the restoration project had increased habitat value for fish and wildlife. They also identified the project as a useful reference for future restoration work involving land managed by different agencies. The research highlights the practical importance of examining ecological changes across many years when evaluating a wetland restoration project.The study draws on records from 1994 to 2022, an elapsed span of 28 years. Its title describes the restoration as a 27-year project, but the available publication details do not specify how that period was calculated. The findings are best understood through the dated observations and the vegetation changes documented over the study period. Rather than establishing a universal pattern for restored wetlands, the Metzger Marsh research documents the course of one project. It records the initial response to lowered water levels, the later dominance of invasive common reed, subsequent management and the prevalence of cattails and other wetland plants by 2022. Together, these observations provide a long-term basis for understanding vegetation change at the site and evaluating restoration management.
Article Summary: Metzger Marsh is a coastal wetland in the western Lake Erie region of Ohio. A dike was built in 1995 to replace a protective barrier beach that had eroded. By 2000, invasive common reed had become dominant. By 2022, cattails and other wetland plants were dominant.

Article Title: Britain built a 70-foot water tower disguised as a house in 1923; its 50,000-gallon tank was damaged by a wartime shell before the landmark became a holiday home
Article Text:
Representative Image of Thorpeness’s whimsical house-shaped water tower surrounded by trees in Suffolk ( AI Generrated Image)

House in the Clouds: how Thorpeness disguised a water tower

Wartime damage changed the water tower’s capacity

From water infrastructure to holiday accommodation

In the English village of Thorpeness, a 70-foot structure built to store water was designed to resemble a house perched above the trees. Completed in 1923, the building concealed a tank with an original capacity of 50,000 gallons, while the structure below provided living accommodation. Known as the House in the Clouds, it was part of the development of Thorpeness, a planned holiday village on the Suffolk coast. Glencairn Stuart Ogilvie, the owner and developer of the Thorpeness Estate, conceived the village and commissioned architects to help realise its distinctive design. Historic England credits Frederick Forbes Glennie with the building’s 1923 design, commissioned as part of Glencairn Stuart Ogilvie’s development of Thorpeness. Its timber weatherboarding, gabled roof and domestic-style windows helped it fit the village’s unusual architectural character. More than a century later, the building remains a landmark, despite no longer serving its original purpose as a water tower. Its survival shows how a practical structure, shaped by whimsy and later adapted for new uses, can become the defining landmark of a planned village’s character.The House in the Clouds was built to provide a water supply for Thorpeness. Its unusual appearance reflected the character of the village, which Ogilvie developed as a holiday destination with buildings designed to create a distinctive landscape rather than a conventional resort. The building’s Historic England listing describes a steel-frame structure clad in weatherboarding, topped by a pantiled, gabled roof. The lower part consists of a five-storey tower, while the upper section, supported by arched corner braces, housed the water tank. Windows were incorporated into the structure, including casement windows and projecting bay windows.The original tank held 50,000 gallons. According to the property’s official history, water was pumped from a well using the neighbouring windmill, with a petrol engine available as an alternative when wind conditions were insufficient. The elevated tank formed part of the water-supply system developed for the village. The building was initially called the Gazebo. Mrs Malcolm Mason, a children’s author and friend of Ogilvie, christened it the House in the Clouds. The property’s history records that a poem she wrote in 1923 was inspired by the building. Its new name captured the appearance of a house seemingly suspended above the surrounding trees. Historic England, which designated the building Grade II listed in 1995, describes it as a landmark and the best-known building in the resort village. Its combination of domestic architecture and water-storage infrastructure has helped preserve its distinctive identity.The building was damaged during the Second World War. According to the property’s official history, an English Bofors anti-aircraft shell passed through the tank’s south-eastern corner in 1943 while the gun was firing at a V1 flying bomb. The shell damaged the tank, and two women, the Miss Humphreys, were occupying the accommodation below and were asleep at the time. The subsequent repairs reduced the tank’s capacity from 50,000 gallons to 30,000 gallons. The property’s history records that sections of the tank’s existing steel were used in the repair. The reduction meant that the tower could hold 20,000 fewer gallons than it had originally been designed to store.The building’s water-supply arrangements also evolved over the following decades. An electric pump replaced the petrol engine in 1953, according to the property’s history. By 1963, a wider water supply had been introduced to the area, although the tank continued to be used for storage for a period afterwards. The tower eventually ceased to serve its original function. The property’s history places the end of its use for local water storage in 1977. The tank itself was removed in 1979, opening the way for the former storage space to become part of the house. Refurbishment of the interior and restoration of the garden began in 1987. These changes allowed the structure to survive beyond the purpose for which it had been built. Rather than remaining a working water tower, it became a house whose unusual upper section no longer needed to accommodate a large volume of water.Today, the House in the Clouds operates as holiday accommodation. Its official accommodation page lists five bedrooms distributed across the second, third and fourth floors, with a games room on the fifth floor. The different levels allow guests to experience a building whose layout developed from its original combination of a water tank and living space. The property stands on Uplands Road in Thorpeness, in Suffolk, close to the village’s golf course and Meare, the artificial lake created as part of the resort’s development. Visitors can find practical details through the property’s official location page.The building’s appeal comes from the contrast between its appearance and its original function. From a distance, its roof and weatherboarded exterior resemble a house elevated above the village. Its history, however, is tied to a practical need: storing and supplying water to the developing community. The House in the Clouds is an example of how infrastructure can become part of a place’s architectural identity. Built in 1923, damaged during wartime, altered when its water-storage role ended, and later adapted for holiday use, it has remained a recognisable feature of Thorpeness. Its original purpose has disappeared, but the structure continues to serve a new one while retaining the appearance that made it unusual in the first place.
Article Summary: The House in the Clouds was part of the development of Thorpeness, a planned holiday village on the Suffolk coast. Completed in 1923, the building concealed a tank with an original capacity of 50,000 gallons, while the structure below provided living accommodation. Its timber weatherboarding, gabled roof and domestic-style windows helped it fit the village's unusual architectural character.

Article Title: Nominee vs legal heir: What is the difference and who has claim on assets? All you need to know
Article Text:
AI image

Who is a Nominee?



Who is a Legal Heir?

Difference between a Nominee and a Legal heir

Aspect Nominee Legal Heir Role Custodian Owner Transfer of Assets Can be done without any legal formalities. Requires testamentary documents for proof of ownership. Powers No power to transact, use, or transfer assets. Power to use and transact assets as an owner. Appointment Owner can appoint anyone, but some institutions specify certain conditions. Determined by succession/personal laws. Legal Right Cannot contest ownership legally. Can contest ownership in a court of law.

When individuals open bank accounts, invest in mutual funds, or buy insurance, they are often asked to name a nominee.However, many people mistakenly assume that the nominee automatically inherits the assets. In reality, the nominee is not always the final recipient — the ownership rights belong to the legal heir, reported ET.Understanding the distinction between these two is essential to ensure that your wealth is passed on to the intended beneficiaries.A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets.The nominee’s role is limited to holding and managing the assets until they are legally transferred to the rightful heirs.According to ET, the nominee cannot sell, trade, or make any transactional decisions about the assets.The account or policy owner can appoint anyone — family, friends, or acquaintances — as a nominee, though financial institutions often prefer close family members.In some cases, the nominee and the legal heir can be the same person, which helps in ensuring a smoother transfer of assets.The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away.To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will or other testamentary proof.If there is no will — a situation known as dying intestate — the heir is determined as per the country’s succession or personal laws, reported ET.While a nominee can initially access the assets, only the legal heir can claim them permanently or challenge ownership in court.Experts quoted by ET emphasise that having clarity on this difference helps avoid disputes and ensures that the savings reach the intended family members or beneficiaries.Therefore, it is advisable to regularly update both nominees and wills to align with one’s estate planning goals.
Article Summary: A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets. The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away. To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will.

How Jeevan Pramaan simplifies pensioner verification



Every year, lakhs of pensioners across India must prove that they are still alive to continue receiving their pension. This verification, known as the Life Certificate or Digital Life Certificate (DLC), is a crucial and mandatory step in ensuring that pension payments are made only to eligible recipients, preventing fraud and misuse.Traditionally, this process involved visiting the bank or pension office in person, standing in long queues, and submitting a signed paper certificate. However, with the government’s focus on digitisation and technological advancement, this process has become much simpler, faster, and more convenient. Pensioners can now submit their certificates digitally from the comfort of their homes using Jeevan Pramaan, a secure, user-friendly, and Aadhaar-based platform.A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries.The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric-enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.Introduced by the Government of India, it uses Aadhaar-based biometric authentication using either fingerprint or iris scan to verify a pensioner’s identity. Once verified, a digital certificate is automatically generated and shared with authorised pension disbursing agencies.This online process eliminates the need for physical verification, providing elderly pensioners with a simpler and more accessible way to maintain their pension benefits.According to PIB, The submission of the Life Certificate is mandatory for all pensioners who wish to continue receiving their pension without interruption. For the year 2025, the standard submission period is betweenTo make the process more comfortable for the elderly, the government allows pensioners aged 80 years and above to begin the submission process earlier, from 1 October 2025. This extended window gives senior citizens more time and flexibility to complete the procedure without facing last-minute difficulties.The Jeevan Pramaan process involves two main steps: registering the biometric device and generating the digital certificate.Before using the service, pensioners or operators must register their biometric device such as a fingerprint or iris scanner. During registration, the user provides their Aadhaar number and mobile number, after which an OTP (One-Time Password) is sent to their mobile. After entering the OTP, they must provide their name and email ID before scanning their fingerprint or iris.Once authentication is complete, the system confirms that device registration was successful, allowing the user to move to the next step.In this step, the pensioner enters personal details such as Aadhaar number, mobile number, name, PPO number, pension type, sanctioning authority, disbursing agency, and bank account details. The system also asks whether the pensioner has remarried or is re-employed.After entering all details, the pensioner scans their fingerprint or iris using the registered biometric device. Upon successful authentication, the Digital Life Certificate is generated, and an SMS acknowledgment with the Jeevan Pramaan Certificate ID is sent to the registered mobile number.This certificate is automatically stored in the Life Certificate Repository, accessible anytime to both pensioners and pension agencies.Once the Digital Life Certificate is created, it can be electronically delivered to the concerned Pension Disbursing Agency (PDA). PDAs can log in to the Jeevan Pramaan portal to view, verify, or download the certificate directly.Pensioners can also download a PDF copy of their certificate by visiting the Jeevan Pramaan website and entering their Pramaan ID or Aadhaar number. This ensures transparency and easy access for future reference.The government provides several options to submit the Life Certificate, allowing pensioners to choose the method that suits them best.Pensioners who prefer traditional methods can visit their bank branch or a Citizen Service Centre (CSC) to submit their Life Certificate physically. Trained staff at these centres assist pensioners in verifying their details and completing the process.For those unable to travel due to age or health issues, India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) offers a doorstep banking service. Pensioners can schedule an appointment, and an IPPB representative will visit their home to complete the submission using biometric authentication. This service is available for both IPPB and non-IPPB account holders.For pensioners comfortable with technology, the Jeevan Pramaan portal provides a completely online process. By visiting https://jeevanpramaan.gov.in, pensioners can submit their Digital Life Certificate using a computer, laptop, or smartphone equipped with a fingerprint or iris scanner.The system uses the Aadhaar platform to authenticate biometric details. Once verification is successful, a Digital Life Certificate is generated and stored in a secure online repository. Pension disbursing agencies can then directly access the certificate, removing the need for physical paperwork.The UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) app offers another easy option. Pensioners can download the app from the Google Play Store, search for “Jeevan Pramaan,” and select “Generate Life Certificate.”After entering the necessary details such as Aadhaar number, PPO number, and type of pension, pensioners must authenticate themselves using biometric verification. The app then generates a Digital Life Certificate (DLC), which is automatically shared with the pension disbursing authority.All pensioners who receive government, defence, or private sector pensions through authorised disbursing agencies are required to submit their Life Certificate every year. This includes:Failure to submit the certificate within the stipulated period may result in temporary suspension of pension payments until verification is completed.To ensure a smooth submission process, pensioners should keep certain details and documents ready. These include:Having these details ready helps to avoid delays or errors during authentication, whether submitting online or offline.Yes, an Aadhaar number or Virtual ID (VID) is mandatory to generate a Digital Life Certificate. The entire Jeevan Pramaan system is based on Aadhaar authentication, which ensures accuracy and prevents fraud. Pensioners must make sure their Aadhaar is linked with their mobile number and bank account before attempting to generate the certificate.The Digital Life Certificate is fully valid and legally recognised under the Information Technology Act. Pension disbursing authorities across India accept it as an official document, equivalent to the traditional paper-based life certificate.Its biometric verification system makes it secure and tamper-proof, reducing the chances of wrongful pension disbursal or misuse of pension funds.Before the introduction of Jeevan Pramaan, pensioners often faced difficulties in submitting their certificates, especially those with health problems or limited mobility. The digital system has removed these challenges, allowing pensioners to submit their verification anytime and anywhere.By integrating biometric technology and Aadhaar authentication, Jeevan Pramaan has streamlined pension management, improving efficiency for both pensioners and government departments. It also enhances transparency and ensures that genuine beneficiaries receive payments on time.
Article Summary: A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries. The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric- enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.

Include property, investments, bank accounts, insurance policies, and any valuable items you own.Decide who will inherit your assets by choosing your beneficiaries. You can assign specific items to each beneficiary and select backup beneficiaries in case your first choices can't inherit. Article Title: How to get your CIBIL credit score without a PAN card
Article Text:
Your credit score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity.

What is a CIBIL score?

How to get your CIBIL Credit score without a PAN Card

Factors affecting your CIBIL score

CIBIL credit score : Understanding your creditworthiness is pivotal in today's financial landscape, especially when seeking loans or credit cards. The Credit Information Bureau (India) Limited, commonly known as CIBIL, plays an important role in this regard by providing credit scores to borrowers.According to ET, credit score helps banks make informed decisions about extending credit cards and loans. Your credit history influences your CIBIL score , which is calculated using a special method.Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.1. Go to the official CIBIL website and click on 'Personal CIBIL score,' then 'Get Your Free CIBIL score.' Follow the link provided and fill in all the required details.2. If you don’t have a PAN Card, you can use an alternative identification such as Passport, Voter ID, Driver’s License, or Ration Card. Enter the number of the chosen ID.3. Provide your date of birth, PIN code, and select your state. Finally, enter your mobile number and click on ‘Accept and Continue’.4. Authenticate your identity by entering the OTP (One-Time Password) delivered to your mobile device on the next screen. Click 'Continue' to proceed.5. Choose whether you want to link the device with your account. Select 'Yes' or 'No' based on your preference.6. Upon successful registration, you will see a page confirming that 'You have successfully registered!'7. Click on ‘Go to Dashboard’ to access and view your CIBIL score.The factors influencing the new CIBIL score, as stated on the CIBIL website, include:1. Depth of credit: This refers to the duration of your existing credit history, calculated from the opening date of your oldest credit account.2. Long-term trend of outstanding balances: The overall trend of outstanding balances over time affects your score.3. Transaction history on credit cards: How you manage transactions on your credit cards impacts your score.4. Ratio of actual repayment amount to total amount due: This ratio indicates your repayment behavior and influences your score accordingly.5. Number of new accounts opened and number of accounts closed: Opening or closing accounts can affect your score, so managing these actions wisely is important.
Article Summary: Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.

Article Title: CERT-In issues 'critical' alert as AI agents access 'confidential' data of Indian firms'
Article Text:
CERT-In issues warning after AI agents accessed live systems and confidential data of organisations without authorisation

AI Agents

as Attack Vectors

AI tools speed up cyberattacks

What organisations should do

NEW DELHI: India’s cybersecurity agency CERT-In has issued a “critical” alert after autonomous artificial intelligence (AI) agents under test accessed live systems and confidential data belonging to Indian organisations without authorisation.The agency has also warned that cybercriminals are using publicly available AI tools to launch attacks faster, leaving businesses with only hours to respond.In an advisory titled, the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) detailed two types of incidents affecting the country's organisations.In the first, AI model providers reported that AI models and agents being tested for research and evaluation had gone beyond their assigned tasks and accessed live systems.The agents were able to read business records containing personal information and confidential material by using credentials and connection settings exposed in application configurations, public code repositories and cloud services with excessive access permissions.A key concern was that none of the affected organisations detected the unauthorised access themselves. The incidents came to light only after the AI model providers disclosed them following internal reviews, CERT-In said as cited by news agency PTI.In a separate set of incidents identified through its own threat monitoring, CERT-In found cybercriminals using publicly available AI-based security tools to scan targets, identify weaknesses and exploit them in financially motivated attacks against Indian entities.These tools were being repackaged and deployed on servers across several countries, the agency said.ALSO READ: Perched in Sikkim, India’s first digital nomad village logs in to local life According to CERT-In, the use of AI-powered tools reduced the time between gaining initial access to a system and causing damage from several days to just a few hours. Organisations that only partially fixed the security weaknesses were targeted again within days, with attacks carried out on a larger scale.The agency said the incidents stemmed from familiar security lapses that AI tools could identify and exploit faster and on a greater scale than human attackers.These included passwords, access keys and other credentials exposed in source code, public repositories, configuration files and web content; outdated or unused application programming interfaces (APIs) still accessible over the internet; payment API keys stored in plain text; and cloud services granting more permissions than necessary.Internet-facing administrative systems, outdated software and weak passwords or the absence of multi-factor authentication also created opportunities for attackers.In some incidents, AI agents retrieved the same exposed credentials again and reused them in separate operations, CERT-In noted.CERT-In has urged organisations to audit their source code, public repositories and their histories, configuration files, client applications and cloud storage to identify exposed credentials. Any compromised credentials should be changed, and sensitive information should be removed from code histories.The agency has also recommended shutting down unused or outdated APIs, limiting cloud access to only what is necessary, removing administrative interfaces from public internet access and enforcing multi-factor authentication.Organisations should monitor systems for suspicious activity and retain logs for at least 180 days.
Article Summary: India's cybersecurity agency CERT-In has issued a ‘critical’ alert after AI agents under test accessed live systems and confidential data belonging to Indian organisations. The agency has also warned that cybercriminals are using publicly available AI tools to launch attacks faster.

Article Title: More adult nappies, more pet prams? What Japan and Korea’s numbers really say
Article Text:
Japan’s adult nappy production and South Korea’s pet-stroller sales reveal shifting demographics (AI-generated image)

When adult nappies overtook baby nappies

illustration

Pet strollers sell more than baby strollers

Two small objects offer a striking glimpse of demographic change in Japan and South Korea: a nappy and a pram. But the numbers behind them answer different questions.In Japan, more than 10 billion adult incontinence products were produced in 2025, against just over 7.1 billion baby nappies. That is a comparison by number of pieces. The adult count includes pads and liners as well as nappies and pants. It measures production, which is not necessarily the same as the number bought or used in Japan.South Korea’s 2025 finding looks similar at first: 61,418 tonnes of adult products supplied, compared with 54,001 tonnes of child products. The adult category overtook the child category by weight in 2024 and stayed ahead in 2025. But a heavier pile need not contain more nappies. Both Korean categories also include hygiene underpads.How different might the count be? One Japanese study calculated an average weight of 62.4g for an adult nappy and 32.1g for a baby nappy. Applying those weights to Korea’s supply gives the following, not an estimate of actual Korean sales:Those weights come from Japan and do not account for the mix of products in Korea’s supply.They cannot establish Korea’s actual piece count. They do show why the distinction matters: adult supply weighs about 14% more, yet could comprise fewer individual products. For adult products to lead by number, their average weight would have to be less than about 14% greater than the child average.The pram finding has a different boundary. On Gmarket, a South Korean online shopping marketplace, pet strollers accounted for 58% of pet and baby stroller sales by number through September 2024; baby strollers accounted for 42%. The result describes sales on Gmarket. It does not tell us which type sold more across every shop in South Korea, or how many homes have pets and children.The three figures are revealing when read precisely: Japan’s adult products lead by pieces produced; Korea’s adult products lead by weight supplied; and pet strollers led on Gmarket. Each captures part of a changing market. The unit and the source determine exactly what we can say about it.
Article Summary: In Japan, more than 10 billion adult incontinence products were produced in 2025, against just over 7.1 billion baby nappies. The adult category overtook the child category by weight in 2024 and stayed ahead in 2025. On Gmarket, a South Korean online shopping marketplace, pet strollers accounted for 58% of pet and baby stroller sales.

Article Title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang ‘strongly’ disagrees with OpenAI’s Sam Altman on AI agents hacking websites, ‘I’m willing to accept no…’
Article Text:
Jensen Huang.

Sam Altman’s acceptable tradeoffs vs. Jensen Huang’s absolute containment

OpenAI’s AI agents hack Hugging Face

Jensen Huang dismisses existential AI doomerism

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has drawn a sharp line against cyber incidents caused by artificial intelligence (AI) agents, insisting the tech sector should have zero tolerance for such breaches. His stance places him in direct opposition to OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman , who recently argued that occasional cyber breaches might be an unavoidable tradeoff for the technology's broader societal gains.“I’m willing to accept no incidents of cybersecurity. We should not accept any of them.We should do everything we can to avoid them,” Huang told Fortune in an interview in London.Huang’s remarks come after statements by Altman suggesting the public must tolerate a degree of digital fallout as AI advances. Earlier this month, Altman told Vanity Fair that society may have to accept “some bad things happening” – including misuse, scams and major cyberattacks – because people will ultimately do “orders of magnitude” more good than harm with the technology.Shortly after, during an appearance on Politico’s Decoded podcast, Altman warned of “a coming tidal wave of cybersecurity problems” originating from rival open-source systems.A few months ago, a swarm of OpenAI's own experimental agents broke out of their training sandbox and breached the Hugging Face platform. Huang flatly rejected the idea that these incidents are the price of progress, arguing that every breach reported so far could have been prevented with stricter oversight and better sandboxing.Comparing the challenge to the early days of the consumer internet, Huang noted that early web browsers initially allowed malicious websites to infect host computers with viruses. The solution was sandboxing: forcing browsers to run websites in isolated containers so they could never access or alter the underlying operating system.According to Huang, autonomous AI agents require the exact same architectural isolation, which is sealed inside secure digital containers to ensure they cannot touch, compromise, or damage anything beyond their strictly authorised operational boundaries.Beyond immediate cybersecurity debates, the Nvidia chief dismissed broader warnings of existential catastrophe voiced by executives across leading labs, such as Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei. Maintaining that the software remains “completely in our control,” Huang questioned the logic of building systems if leaders genuinely believe they pose an extinction threat.“I don’t know why anybody would want to support the advancement of a technology that’s going to result, you know, in the end of human civilization as we know it. And so, if they believe that, they really ought to stop working on it,” Huang said.
Article Summary: Jensen Huang says tech sector should have zero tolerance for cyber incidents caused by artificial intelligence (AI) agents. His stance places him in direct opposition to OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman, who recently argued that occasional cyber breaches might be an unavoidable tradeoff for the technology's broader societal gains.

Article Title: Researchers equip giant cockroaches with medical backpacks, fitted with cameras and syringes, the cyborgs search trapped survivors to deliver life-saving aid in disasters
Article Text:
Image credit: X (Twitter)

How these cyborg cockroaches work

What the tests reveal about the technology

How search and rescue teams could use them

Giant cockroaches could help rescue survivors after disasters. Researchers in Australia are developing cyborg-like insects equipped with miniature backpacks containing cameras, electronics and syringe systems designed to deliver emergency medication. The technology aims to help search-and-rescue teams locate injured people trapped beneath rubble and provide medical assistance when direct access is difficult.Called “paraborgs,” these modified insects combine their natural ability to navigate confined spaces with remotely controlled equipment. Scientists are testing whether the cockroaches can carry medical supplies into hazardous areas, identify potential victims through camera feeds and deliver drugs to targets. The approach could eventually support emergency responders dealing with collapsed buildings, earthquakes and other disasters where time and access are critical.According to a BGR report, the project involves researchers associated with the University of Queensland and the University of New South Wales. By combining insect movement with miniature electronic systems, the team aims to reach places conventional rescue equipment may struggle to access.The project uses the giant burrowing cockroach, scientifically known as Macropanesthia rhinoceros, a large cockroach species native to Australia. Its size makes it suitable for carrying a small electronic backpack containing a camera, control equipment and a syringe-based delivery mechanism.Unlike conventional robotic devices, these insects retain their natural ability to move through tight spaces. Researchers use implanted electrodes to stimulate the cockroaches' nervous systems, letting operators remotely control their direction. This could help guide them through gaps in collapsed structures and other areas human rescuers cannot easily enter.The cameras mounted on their backs provide a view of the surrounding environment. Rescue teams could use these images to assess obstacles, identify accessible routes and look for people who may be trapped nearby.The medical delivery system is another part of the design. Researchers have developed a mechanism that can fire a small syringe, described as functioning like a dart gun, towards a target. The aim is to deliver medication when a person needs urgent treatment and a medical professional cannot reach them immediately.Potential applications include delivering drugs to people experiencing certain emergencies, such as snakebite or severe allergic reactions. However, the technology remains experimental, and using it in real disaster rescue operations would require further testing.Early testing has examined whether the cockroaches can reach designated checkpoints and successfully deliver medication using the syringe mechanism.According to the reported results, the insects reached the checkpoints with a 100% success rate. The syringe system recorded a 72% success rate when delivering medication to targets. When the syringe was fired from within six inches of a target, the success rate increased to 95%.These results indicate that the insects can navigate designated routes under test conditions, while the distance between the syringe and its target remains an important factor in delivery accuracy.The findings also highlight the distinction between successfully guiding an insect to a location and delivering medicine accurately. In a real emergency, researchers would need to account for uneven terrain, limited visibility, unpredictable movement, and the injured person's condition.Further development would also be necessary to establish how the equipment performs in different environments and whether the system can deliver medication safely and consistently.Search and rescue operations often involve locating people in unstable buildings, collapsed structures and debris-filled areas. Sending rescuers into these environments can be difficult because of restricted access, falling material and the possibility of further structural collapse.Small insects equipped with cameras could provide another way to inspect such locations before a human rescuer enters. Their ability to move through narrow gaps could help teams gather information about spaces that are difficult to examine using larger equipment.Time is another consideration. Finding an injured person quickly can affect the treatment they receive, especially when the emergency involves a condition that requires prompt medical attention. Camera-equipped cockroaches could help rescuers assess a location and identify a possible route towards someone who needs assistance.The technology may also help reduce the physical demands placed on rescue workers. Rather than manually clearing every accessible section of debris, teams could first use the insects to inspect selected areas and determine where further intervention is needed.However, the system would not replace conventional rescue personnel or medical treatment. Its effectiveness would depend on camera visibility, remote control, access to the target, and the ability to safely deliver the appropriate medication.For now, the research demonstrates a potential application of biohybrid technology, which combines living organisms with electronic systems. If further testing establishes its reliability and safety, these cyborg cockroaches could become an additional tool for locating and assisting disaster survivors in places where conventional rescue equipment has limited access.
Article Summary: Researchers in Australia are developing cyborg-like insects equipped with miniature backpacks containing cameras, electronics and syringe systems. The technology aims to help search-and-rescue teams locate injured people trapped beneath rubble and provide medical assistance when direct access is difficult. Scientists are testing whether the cockroaches can carry medical supplies into hazardous areas.

Article Title: Meta AI head Alexandr Wang praises Mark Zuckerberg, he replies: I have never gotten such a nice…
Article Text:
Mark Zuckerberg and Alexandr Wang

‘ Very Bayesian ’: Rapid decisive conviction

Meta AI head Alexandr Wang and company CEO Mark Zuckerberg recently had a candid exchange on the company's executive leadership and high-stakes decision-making. During a recent interview, Meta’s Wang was asked about the qualities of Facebook founder, and he offered glowing praise for Zuckerberg, highlighting his exceptional willingness to make massive, rapid pivots based on core convictions. During the conversation Wang was specifically asked how Zuckerberg differed as a leader from what he initially anticipated. Before Wang could reply, Zuckerberg opened with a lighthearted quip, joking, “I think I can leave now.” Wang quickly followed up with his perspective on their working relationship over the past year.Wang noted that while he does not have an extensive set of comparisons, observing Zuckerberg's management style firsthand revealed unique traits that stand out even within elite tech founder circles:“One of the very cool things about working with Mark over the past year has just been watching the true degree of his boldness,” Wang explained, adding, “Once he internalises certain beliefs, like the speed and magnitude of willing to change prior actions and pivot towards the worldview that is consistent with those beliefs, I think these are pretty unusual traits, generally speaking, even among this base of founders. Very Bayesian.”The analytical praise drew a warm, humorous reaction from Zuckerberg.“Very Bayesian. I've never gotten such a nice compliment,” Zuckerberg responded.A person who follows the Bayesian method relies on statistical inference, using Bayes' theorem to update the probability of a hypothesis as new data or evidence becomes available.Expanding on his observations, Wang admitted that Zuckerberg's appetite for sweeping strategic gambles initially took him by surprise before earning his deep respect.“No, but then I think also just the degree of boldness. It was actually quite puzzling to me at first, the degree to which you were willing to make these massive bets. That is quite a notable trait and something I really admire,” Wang continued.Zuckerberg concluded the exchange with appreciation for the assessment, replying: “I'm so flattered.”
Article Summary: Meta AI head Alexandr Wang and Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg recently had a candid exchange on the company's executive leadership and high-stakes decision- making. Article Title: Microsoft fixes 1,411 vulnerabilities in record October 2026 security update
Article Text:
Microsoft Windows 11

Breakdown by vulnerability type

Elevation of Privilege: 677 vulnerabilities

Remote Code Execution: 317 vulnerabilities

Information Disclosure: 254 vulnerabilities

Denial of Service: 73 vulnerabilities

Security Feature Bypass: 40 vulnerabilities

Spoofing: 28 vulnerabilities

Microsoft security patch: Three zero-days addressed

End of support deadlines for Windows 11 and Windows 10

Microsoft has released its October 2026 Patch Tuesday security rollout, delivering fixes for a record-breaking 1,411 vulnerabilities, including one actively exploited zero-day and two publicly disclosed zero-day flaws. The huge volume of fixes comes as Microsoft increasingly leans on artificial intelligence (AI) platforms to discover and remediate security bugs across its software ecosystem. The monthly release addresses 70 “Critical” vulnerabilities, consisting of 57 Remote Code Execution flaws, 11 Elevation of Privilege issues and 2 spoofing bugs.The tally counts only updates released directly on Patch this week itself, excluding 348 separate flaws resolved earlier this month across Azure API Center, Azure App Service, Azure Event Grid, Azure SRE Agent, Mariner, Microsoft Bookings, Microsoft Dataverse, Microsoft Exchange Server and Microsoft Partner Center.Across the release, elevation of privilege and remote execution bugs made up the vast majority of the patched flaws:Microsoft defines a zero-day vulnerability as a flaw that has been publicly disclosed or actively exploited before an official patch exists. The October update resolves three such weaknesses. In one case, attackers actively exploited this flaw to evade Windows' “Mark of the Web” security mechanism.Microsoft warned that “improper neutralization of special elements used in a command ('command injection') in Windows Shell allows an unauthorized attacker to bypass a security feature over a network. ”The second local security bypass flaw was discovered by James Forshaw of Google Project Zero, and allows authenticated attackers to subvert Windows Defender Application Control (WDAC) and launch unauthorized applications.Thirdly, the flaw is caused by improperly controlled sequential memory allocation within .NET, and enables unauthorised attackers to trigger a denial-of-service condition over a network. Microsoft did not disclose who reported the vulnerability.Alongside the security updates, Microsoft formally marked end-of-support milestones for multiple operating system editions:“Today, October 13, 2026, Windows 11, version 24H2 Home and Pro, and Windows 10 Enterprise LTSB 2016 have reached end of updates. The October 2026 monthly security update is the last update available for these editions,” Microsoft stated.
Article Summary: Microsoft has released its October 2026 Patch Tuesday security rollout, delivering fixes for a record-breaking 1,411 vulnerabilities. The huge volume of fixes comes as Microsoft increasingly leans on artificial intelligence (AI) platforms to discover and remediate security bugs. The monthly release addresses 70 “Critical” vulnerabilities, consisting of 57 Remote Code Execution flaws, 11 Elevation of Privilege issues and 2 spoofing bugs.

Article Title: Government issues critical warning as AI agents access Indian companies' confidential data
Article Text:
Representative image

CERT-In shares two incidents of AI models accessing company data without authorisation

AI tools cut cyberattack timelines from days to hours

CERT-In's advice to companies and AI developers

India’s cybersecurity agency, CERT-In has issued a 'critical' advisory warning artificial intelligence (AI) agents have accessed live systems and confidential data of companies without authorisation. In its advisory titled ‘AI Agents as Attack Vectors’, the cyber agency said that threat actors are actively weaponising open-source agentic AI tools to execute rapid cyberattacks. It highlighted two distinct categories of incidents targeting the Information and Communication Technology (ICT) infrastructure of Indian entities.In one case, AI agents accessed business records containing personal and confidential information. In another, cybercriminals used AI-powered tools to find security gaps and launch financially motivated attacks against Indian organisations.During these incidents, the AI agents accessed business records containing personal data and confidential information. They used credentials and connection settings that had been left exposed in application configurations, public code repositories and cloud service roles with excessive permissions, the agency said.Notably, none of the affected organisations detected the unauthorised access themselves, PTI reported.According to CERT-In, the use of AI agents has sharply reduced the time between gaining initial access to a system and causing damage. In the campaign it identified, the gap shrank from several days to a few hours.Organisations that only partly fixed the security weaknesses were attacked again within days, with the attacks carried out on a larger scale, the agency said. CERT-In noted that basic security failures were behind all the recent AI agent-driven incidents it observed. These included passwords, access keys and other credentials exposed in source code, public repositories, configuration files, client applications and publicly accessible web content.Other weaknesses included old or test application programming interfaces (APIs) that remained accessible over the internet, payment API keys stored in plain text, cloud systems with excessive permissions, and management interfaces exposed to the internet.Unpatched software, weak passwords and a lack of multi-factor authentication also left systems vulnerable. AI agents were able to find and exploit these gaps faster and on a larger scale than human attackers.To reduce these risks, CERT-In has asked organisations to check their source code, public repositories and their commit histories, configuration files, client applications and cloud storage for exposed credentials. The agency has recommended that companies change exposed credentials and remove them from code histories. They should also shut down unused, outdated and test APIs, limit cloud access to only what is required, take administrative interfaces off the public internet and enforce multi-factor authentication.Organisations have also been advised to monitor systems for attacks and retain logs for at least 180 days.CERT-In said companies should treat their systems as compromised after a credential leak or confirmed intrusion until a forensic investigation clears them. They should also prepare for repeat attack attempts within days or weeks.For AI developers, research laboratories and evaluation agencies, the agency recommended isolating research and testing environments. Outbound network access should be blocked except where a task specifically requires it, with restrictions enforced at the network level rather than through instructions given to the AI model.It also advised using synthetic targets and test credentials instead of real production data during research and evaluation.
Article Summary: India’s cybersecurity agency, CERT-In has issued a 'critical' advisory warning artificial intelligence (AI) agents have accessed live systems and confidential data of companies without authorisation. The agency said that threat actors are actively weaponising open-source agentic AI tools to execute rapid cyberattacks.

Article Title: Some Accenture employees spent $1,000 a month on Anthropic’s Claude AI, company will now centrally fund $29, projects to cover the rest; memo says: All costs are...
Article Text:
$29 a month: Accenture’s new Claude limit

Anything above $29 now gets charged to a project budget

Heavy Claude Code users are scrambling for Premium upgrades

Accenture joins Microsoft and Meta in pushing back on tokenmaxxing

Accenture, one of the world’s largest consulting firms and a vocal champion of AI adoption among its clients, has changed how it pays for its own employees’ use of Anthropic’s Claude. According to an internal announcement seen by 404 Media, the company will now centrally fund $29 a month per person towards Claude Enterprise usage, effective October 1. Employees can keep using Claude beyond that amount, with the extra cost charged internally to the relevant project or team.That central amount is small next to what some staff have been spending. Several employees have told colleagues internally that their monthly bills run between $500 and $1,000, largely from heavy use of Claude Code. For those on the General plan, all of that additional usage will now be billed to project budgets.The memo states that all Claude costs are now consumption-based. Any usage beyond the central allowance has to be funded through a Work Breakdown Structure, or WBS, which is Accenture's internal billing code for a specific project or team.Employees on the Premium plan are better placed, since it includes $250 worth of token usage every week.Most of the workforce, however, sits on the General plan.The memo also makes clear that a licence is not permanent. Access is tied to role and business need, allocations are reviewed periodically, and licences can be moved to wherever the company feels they deliver the most value. Even supplying a WBS code does not guarantee continued access.Internal messages viewed by 404 Media show how the change has landed. One employee said their usage had crossed $500 for several months in a row and asked how to fast-track a move to Premium, adding that the upgrade option appeared blocked on the support page. Their concern was simple: the extra spend would now hit project costs.Another employee uses Claude Code extensively to build and test an AI accelerator meant for several Accenture clients. Their monthly usage typically sits between $500 and $1,000. "Honestly, this is disappointing," they wrote. A third employee said their access to the tool had been revoked altogether.An Accenture spokesperson told 404 Media that the company makes AI available to all its people and aims to match the right tool to the right work, while continuing to invest in AI capabilities and skills.Accenture is not the first big company to rethink open-ended AI budgets. Microsoft introduced division-level token budgets in July and switched its internal default to a cheaper model, with CoreAI EVP Jay Parikh telling staff that "tokenmaxxing is not what we are optimizing for." Months earlier, its Experiences and Devices group cancelled most Claude Code licences and moved engineers to GitHub Copilot CLI.Tokenmaxxing describes employees burning through as many AI tokens as possible to look productive on usage dashboards. At Meta, an internal leaderboard called "Claudeonomics" ranked staff by token consumption before being pulled within days. Amazon, Uber, Walmart and AT&T have also capped or throttled employee AI spending this year.For a firm that has spent years urging clients to pour money into AI, Accenture’s new funding model shows where the conversation inside companies is heading. Heavy usage alone no longer justifies the bill, and teams are now expected to show what every dollar of tokens actually delivers.
Article Summary: Accenture will now centrally fund $29 a month per person towards Claude Enterprise usage, effective October 1. Employees can keep using Claude beyond that amount, with the extra cost charged internally to the relevant project or team. Several employees have told colleagues internally that their monthly bills run between $500 and $1,000.

Article Title: As Elon Musk shows 'flying Tesla'; says, 'My OG Roadster is still orbiting Mars and Earth'; Meta AI head Alexandr Wang asks: Who is ...
Article Text:
Image credit: Tesla

Meta AI head Alexandr Wang reacts to Tesla’s flying car

Tesla’s ‘flying car’ to go into production in 2028

Tesla CEO Elon Musk unveiled what it calls a ‘flying car’ at a Texas test facility belonging to SpaceX. Musk showed off Tesla’s new Roadster, a two-person sports car that could go from 0 to 60 mph in a record time of less than a second. He said that the car uses suction underneath it to climb up a steep ramp and hang upside down before spinning off the ramp, flipping in the air and using air jets to land. Soon after the demo, Musk shared a post on X (formerly known as Twitter) writing: “My OG Roadster is still orbiting Mars and Earth”. He was replying to a Tesla post juxtaposing the 2018 image of the original Roadster in space aboard a SpaceX Falcon Heavy with a new-generation Roadster featuring integrated cold-gas thrusters from SpaceX.“From Roadster in a rocket. To rocket in a Roadster,” Tesla wrote on X.The demo video of Tesla’s flying Car caught the attention of Meta AI head Alexandr Wang. He posted a humorous reaction questioning the driver in a Tesla stunt video:“wait who the hell was driving the tesla”, Alexandr Wang replied.The Tesla live video showed a futuristic car executing extreme nighttime maneuvers including vertical ramp ascents, jumps with blue thrusters, and smoky landings.Wang’s edited video showcased a fluffy white animated character (likely to be Meta’s Muse) sitting at the steering wheel.Tesla’s flying car or the next-generation Roadster electric uses 10 nozzles and what Elon Musk described as “ultra high-pressure air tanks” to propel itself, both in the air, and to accelerate quickly when on the ground. He described the technology as “the results of what happens when you have a collaboration with the world’s best car company and the world’s best rocket company.”Speaking during the demonstration held at a SpaceX test site in McGregor, Texas, Elon Musk said that the car will go into production in 2028.
Article Summary: Tesla CEO Elon Musk unveiled what it calls a ‘flying car’ at a Texas test facility belonging to SpaceX. Musk showed off Tesla’s new Roadster, a two-person sports car that could go from 0 to 60 mph in a record time of less than a second. The company said the prepaid family plan seeks to bring a family-oriented experience, traditionally associated with postpaid services, to the prepaid segment.

Article Title: Google Brain co-founder Andrew Ng to Dario Amodei, Sam Altman and Elon Musk: ‘You are making up safety arguments.. there is no…’
Article Text:
Andrew Ng, DeepLearning AI founder and co-founder of Google Brain

‘Made-up safety arguments are being used to hurt rivals’

Andrew Ng, the artificial intelligence (AI) pioneer who co-founded Google Brain, has pushed back against apocalyptic warnings that AI could cause human extinction. The founder of DeepLearning AI that provides technical training on Generative AI, Machine Learning, Deep Learning and other topics, accused the industry leaders of manufacturing existential safety arguments to lobby for regulations that crush open-source competition. Speaking in an interview on The Economist’s “Inside Tech” podcast, the AI pioneer dismissed the notion that this technology presents an existential threat to society.“I think there are no meaningful human existential risks from AI. So, efforts to stave off human existential risk seem unnecessary,” Ng said. His remarks are a counterweight to warnings by prominent tech executives and researchers who have embraced so-called “doomerism” – the belief that future super-intelligent machines will slip beyond human control, seize essential infrastructure and wipe out humanity.Ng, a former Stanford University professor who also co-founded Coursera, argued that catastrophic narratives are actively derailing sensible policy while serving the commercial interests of legacy tech incumbents. As per a report in The New York Post, Ng reflected on regulatory debates that gained momentum in 2023, saying that he was taken aback by “the intensity of the lobbying efforts to use made-up safety arguments by a handful of businesses to get regulators to pass bad regulations to stifle competition.According to Ng, technology firms pouring billions of dollars into proprietary, closed-source AI systems have an obvious financial incentive to suppress open-weight, downloadable models that developers can access and run for free.In September, Jacob Coxon, an Anthropic researcher claimed that AI is being developed at a very fast pace and that there is around 10% chances that there is a possibility of human extinction. Following his claims, company CEO Dario Amodei wrote in an online essay that companies should reduce the pace of AI development.He said that the risks associated with developing AI at such a fast pace were “serious”. The bosses of two rival AI firms, Sam Altman of OpenAI and Elon Musk , both agreed with Amodei.Ng also condemned the frequent comparison of AI to nuclear armaments, calling the comparison irresponsible.“One blows up cities; the other is intelligence. What’s [one have] to do with each other?” Ng remarked.By focusing on extreme extinction scenarios, Ng warned that policymakers are being diverted from addressing clear, present-day digital harms: “Regulators are distracted fighting phantoms rather than looking at the actual problems of AI.”Further, despite rapid generative AI gains over recent years, Ng emphasised that the technology remains a long way off from Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) – the level where software can match human capabilities across every intellectual task.
Article Summary: Andrew Ng, the artificial intelligence (AI) pioneer who co-founded Google Brain, has pushed back against apocalyptic warnings that AI could cause human extinction. The founder of DeepLearning AI that provides technical training on Generative AI, Machine Learning, Deep Learning and other topics, accused the industry leaders of manufacturing existential safety arguments.

Article Title: How OpenAI's office spy case 'proves' that spying is not Sam Altman's problem alone and why Google, Anthropic and other AI companies too should be worried
Article Text:
OpenAI’s office spy case has Google and Anthropic on alert too

OpenAI says its own AI models helped catch the alleged office spy

OpenAI warns employees about playground spies and honey traps

Trillion-dollar valuations make Google, Anthropic and OpenAI bigger spy targets

A listening device worth about $13, hidden behind a TV in an OpenAI executive conference room, has become a warning for the entire AI industry. The ChatGPT maker's case against a former engineer, now charged by US federal prosecutors, shows how valuable AI secrets have become and how cheaply someone can try to reach them.OpenAI is also not alone in bracing for this. According to a report by The Wall Street Journal, employees at Google and Anthropic have received similar warnings about spies, honey traps and strangers who ask too many questions. Security experts quoted in the report believe this arrest is unlikely to be the last.Abdulrahman Alfozan, a 35-year-old Saudi national and US permanent resident, joined OpenAI as an engineer in July 2025. Prosecutors allege he wrapped a Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32-S3 Sense, a thumb-sized board with a microphone and camera, in toilet paper and plugged it into a USB port behind the TV.Only executives and their assistants could book the room. It hosted leadership meetings, product sessions and briefings with government officials. OpenAI found the device during a security sweep on September 30 and says it used its own models to trace it to the employee.The FBI arrested him on October 9.He faces one charge of intercepting oral communications, which carries up to five years in prison. OpenAI says it has no sign of him accessing model weights, source code or customer data. His lawyer called the allegations "wholly out of character", adding that his client is not charged with stealing trade secrets.As per WSJ, OpenAI's internal training has been preparing staff for moments like this. One scenario describes a stranger at a San Francisco playground who befriends an employee there with their child, makes small talk and slowly steers it toward work. The stranger is a spy.Employees are told not to wear company-branded clothing outside office, to use privacy screen protectors on public transport and to wipe whiteboards after meetings in case cleaning staff are compromised. Some sessions cover "honey pots", where agents use romance to get close to a target. Staff at Google and Anthropic have been briefed along similar lines.The money explains the nerves. OpenAI and Anthropic are each expected to seek valuations of over $1 trillion when they go public. Phil Venables, former security chief at Google Cloud, told WSJ that the huge cost of training foundation models makes them even more valuable intellectual property.Rapid hiring adds to the risk. AI labs have added thousands of people in a short time, and engineers hop between rivals often. "Catching one guy means there are half a dozen out there," Randy Watt, president of security consultancy SRW, told the publication. Aviv Nahum, CEO of insider-risk startup Above Security, questioned whether security checks are keeping pace with that growth.The industry has been here before. In January, a former Google engineer was convicted of stealing AI trade secrets for China. In 2022, a former Twitter employee was jailed for spying for Saudi Arabia.OpenAI caught its device within days of it being planted. For Google, Anthropic and every other lab chasing a trillion-dollar valuation, the bigger worry is what their own sweeps have not found yet.
Article Summary: A listening device worth about $13, hidden behind a TV in an OpenAI executive conference room, has become a warning for the entire AI industry. The ChatGPT maker's case against a former engineer, now charged by US federal prosecutors, shows how valuable AI secrets have become. Staff at Google and Anthropic have received similar warnings about spies, honey traps and strangers who ask too many questions.
